g.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Dot: estimate at the main XGBoost tuning setting. Thin line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Thick line: 99% interval (the ERA5 study's own is 99.5%). Dashed rules: no difference, and the smallest improvement worth acting on (0.1 points of capacity). Panel 1 and the last panel are differences. The error panels show each set's error. The IFS rows are only the months AIFS Single also covers, March 2025 to April 2026. MARS-only: 12 ERA5 variables that ECMWF's MARS archive serves and that Open-Meteo does not. The ERA5 study fitted those on a different row set, so the two gains are not on equal rows. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar. F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective energy (CAPE), convective inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface temperature, snow, precipitation, pressure, wind, gusts. IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day. FB: F0 plus AIFS Single (ECMWF's machine-learned forecast) radiation and temperature. F6B: F6 plus the same two. Negative control: the arm's columns, with the new variables replaced by copies shuffled among the hours that share a farm, a month, and an hour of day, so only each month's mean at each hour survives. Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before. Planned: written into the study plan before any result existed. Lead days 1 to 3 are pooled. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons. Panel 1 is planned. The error panels and the last panel are exploratory.'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. CAMS:
satellite irradiance service.
Dot: estimate at the main XGBoost tuning setting. Thin line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Thick line:
99% interval (the ERA5 study's own is 99.5%). Dashed rules: no difference, and the smallest improvement worth
acting on (0.1 points of capacity).
Panel 1 and the last panel are differences. The error panels show each set's error.
The IFS rows are only the months AIFS Single also covers, March 2025 to April 2026.
MARS-only: 12 ERA5 variables that ECMWF's MARS archive serves and that Open-Meteo does not. The ERA5 study fitted
those on a different row set, so the two gains are not on equal rows.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar.
F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and
high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective
energy (CAPE), convective inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface temperature, snow,
precipitation, pressure, wind, gusts.
IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day.
FB: F0 plus AIFS Single (ECMWF's machine-learned forecast) radiation and temperature. F6B: F6 plus the same two.
Negative control: the arm's columns, with the new variables replaced by copies shuffled among the hours that share
a farm, a month, and an hour of day, so only each month's mean at each hour survives.
Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before.
Planned: written into the study plan before any result existed. Lead days 1 to 3 are pooled.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
Panel 1 is planned. The error panels and the last panel are exploratory.
